1.
Case called out.

No one appeared on behalf of the respondent no. 2 to oppose the present appeal despite name of Shri Abhishek Srivastava, Advocate being printed in the cause list as counsel for the respondent no. 2. .
2. In the aforesaid background of the case, this Court proceeds hear the instant appeal.

3. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and Shri Ajay Kumar Srivastava, learned A.G.A. for the State-respondent.
4.

The present appeal has been filed under Section 14-A (2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act, 1989 against the impugned order dated 23.08.2023 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act,

sentences.text:
Lakhimpur Kheri in Bail Application No. 417 of 2023 arising out of Case Crime No. 373 of 2023,
under Sections 376(2)(n), 377, 452, 504, 506 , 342, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act,
P.S. Phool Beharh, District - Kheri.

5. Pressing the present appeal and impeaching the order, under appeal, dated 23.08.2023, learned counsel for the appellant stated that the FIR implicating the appellant, aged about 21 years, lodged by the victim/informant, aged about 29 years, a married lady, making allegations to attract Section 376 and other sections of IPC as also Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act is completely false and concocted and was lodged only to extract the financial benefit from the State Exchequer available in the relevant statutes.

6. In continuation, he further submitted that the victim was married to a person who permanently resides at Village-Kachiyani, Police Station- Hyderabad, District - Kheri but the victim resides almost permanently with her parents in the vicinity/village i.e. Village Rajaram Purwa, Mazara Sarwa, Police Station - Phool Bheharh, District - Kheri and of this village, the appellant is a permanent resident and it appears that she was facing financial crisis as such, she lodged the FIR and to fortify the contents/averments made in the FIR has also levelled allegations before the Investigating Officer as also before the Court concerned but to support the story of the prosecution,
there is no medical evidence as upon due medical examination, the doctor concerned opined that there is no use of force, as appears from Annexure No. 3 to the memo of appeal which is a copy of the medico-legal report.

7. He further submitted that the story in the FIR as also the assertion of the victim are false and concocted and the same can also be deduced from the facts that the alleged crime was committed by the appellant on 05.02.2023 and after huge delay the application before the police authority was made on 30.05.2023 and thereafter with further delay an application dated 30.07.2023 under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was preferred and from this these facts, it can also be deduced that after due consultation, the FIR was lodged against the appellant whose particulars are known to the victim as she resides in the same vicinity.
8.

He further submitted that the story of making video clip while committing rape is completely false, as it is improbable as also that the prosecution during the investigation has not collected any evidence to support the allegations pertaining to making video clip and further making calls in regard to the informant after alleged commission of crime by the appellant, there is no evidence.

9. He lastly stated that in the aforesaid background of the case, the appellant, who is in jail since 01.08.2023 and having no criminal history, is entitled for bail and the impugned order is liable to be set aside and the appeal is liable to be allowed.
10. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer of the appellant, however, he could not dispute the above contentions made by the appellant's counsel.

11. Considered the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant-applicant, learned A.G.A., and gone through the contents of the appeal, impugned order, F.I.R., medical report as well Karan Yadav vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Upon due consideration of above facts and circumstances including the medical opinion, and the age of the victim i.e. 29 years and her status, age of the appellant i.e. 21 years, facts pertaining to the place of residence of the victim as also the period of incarceration and also keeping in view the fact that the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, this Court is of the view that the appeal has substance and it is accordingly, allowed.

sentences.text:
14. Let appellant Karan Yadav, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following additional conditions :-
(i) The appellant will cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) The appellant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
(iii) The appellant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(es).
(iv) The appellant shall not commit an offence.

(v) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(vi) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through counsel.
(vii) The appellant will not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.

(viii) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
15.

In case of default of above conditions, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law Karan Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, Lko ...
